stories.title: US / Israel – Iran
stories.detail: 11 headlines. Not enough history yet to say whether that is unusual - the baseline needs 7 days.
stories.why: The one flashpoint that hits gold through every channel at once. Safe-haven bid on the headline, Treasuries bid so nominal and real yields fall, and - uniquely - a credible threat to the Strait of Hormuz spikes crude, which lifts inflation expectations. Roughly a fifth of seaborne oil passes through that strait.
stories.counterweight: The dollar is also a haven, so risk-off bids the dollar too and cancels part of gold's gain. This is why some escalation days produce a far smaller gold move than the headlines imply.
stories.duration: Days. Gold spikes on the exchange of fire and gives most of it back within a week unless the oil disruption is real and sustained, because only then does it reach the Fed's reaction function.

asia.read: Asian equities are broadly lower, averaging -0.69%. Risk came off overnight, which normally gives gold a small bid into London. Gold moved +1.03% overnight in a 2.16% range, and comes into London near the middle of it. Mid-range is the least informative place it can be. 4 minor Asian releases overnight, none of them the kind that reaches gold.
asia.caveat: Measured from 00:00 UK to 21:22. Tokyo closes around 07:00 UK and Hong Kong around 09:00, so this is a session finishing rather than one that has finished.

correlations.regime: Gold and the dollar are running at -0.53. That is the textbook inverse relationship, so dollar moves are doing real work on the price. Against the S&P it is +0.31. Gold is trading WITH risk assets rather than against them, so it is behaving as a liquidity asset right now, not a hedge - do not rely on it to offset an equity drawdown while that holds.

flashpoints.name: Trade and tariffs
flashpoints.spoken_why: Tariffs raise prices and slow growth at the same time, which is the hardest combination for the Federal Reserve to answer.
flashpoints.why_gold: Indirect but real. Tariffs are an inflation impulse and a growth drag at once, which is the hardest combination for the Fed and therefore raises uncertainty about the rate path.
flashpoints.counterweight: Also dollar-positive in the short run, which works against gold. The net effect is genuinely ambiguous and often small.
flashpoints.typical_duration: Weeks, when it changes the inflation outlook. Announcement headlines alone rarely stick.
flashpoints.escalation_markers: Rates above expectations, retaliation, or extension to critical minerals and energy.
flashpoints.summary: 2 headlines. Not enough history yet to say whether that is unusual - the baseline needs 7 days.

flashpoints.name: China / Taiwan
flashpoints.spoken_why: Routine drills mean nothing, but a genuine blockade would be the largest single risk in this market.
flashpoints.why_gold: Low frequency, very high severity. A genuine blockade or invasion scenario is the largest single tail risk in the gold market, because it would be a global supply-chain and reserve-currency event simultaneously.
flashpoints.counterweight: Routine incursions and drills are so frequent they carry almost no information. Gold ignores them, correctly.
flashpoints.typical_duration: Drills: nothing. A real blockade: a regime change in gold pricing, not a spike.
flashpoints.escalation_markers: Quarantine or blockade language, live-fire exercises encircling the island, US carrier movements, or semiconductor export emergencies.
flashpoints.summary: 4 headlines. Not enough history yet to say whether that is unusual - the baseline needs 7 days.
